sources.authors: Tomohiro Hirano, Keiichi Kishi, Alexis Akira Toda
sources.title: Technological Innovation and Bursting Bubbles
sources.method: Theoretical two-period OLG numerical illustration; no estimated population/sample; date length not annualized.
sources.mismatches: Closed economy; post-switch exponents positive in illustration whereas V6 zero-exponent specialization fixes its b and W exponents. Same u technological definitions permit scenario comparison only.

sources.title: Rare Disasters and Asset Markets in the Twentieth Century
sources.method: Historical frequency calibration from 60 large contractions in 35 countries over roughly the twentieth century, using cumulative real per-capita GDP falls of at least 15%; representative-agent Lucas-tree economy with recurring jump disasters.
sources.classification: data-based frequency calibration; p=.025 is model robustness, not confidence bound
sources.mapping: Source model uses Poisson jump intensity p; pi_V6=exp(-p*Delta) is survival over Delta years only if event definitions are equated.
sources.mismatches: Repeated macro disasters, GDP threshold and global historical population are not a one-time absorbing end of a US innovation regime.

sources.authors: Robert J. Barro, José F. Ursúa
sources.title: Macroeconomic Crises since 1870
sources.venue: Brookings Papers on Economic Activity, Spring, 255-350 including discussion
sources.method: Peak-to-trough cumulative declines >=10%; annual series starting as early as1870, 24 consumption countries,36 GDP countries; disasters divided by normal-state years.
sources.classification: empirical conditional transition frequencies; cross-definition values not sampling confidence interval
sources.mapping: pi_V6=(1-h)^Delta under constant annual conditional hazard and a matched absorbing event. Source pi=.277/.287 is disaster EXIT probability and must NOT be copied to V6 pi.
sources.mismatches: Events recur and end; sample mixes war and other contractions; their transition p applies only while normal. New financial regime/technology definitions need distinct data.

sources.authors: Nicholas Bloom, Charles I. Jones, John Van Reenen, Michael Webb
sources.title: Are Ideas Getting Harder to Find?
sources.method: Growth-accounting ratios, not causal marginal-product estimates: idea-output growth divided by effective researchers; aggregate input IPP spending deflated by skilled wages, decadal TFP output; industry/product/firm cases.
sources.classification: descriptive accounting evidence; lambda=.75 robustness is imposed
sources.mapping: Their a_t=(dot A/A)/S resembles V6 a only after identifying A with N and matching research units; their beta in dot A/A=alpha*A^(-beta)*S is a research-productivity elasticity, not V6 saving beta or augmentation exponents xi/nu.
sources.mismatches: Knowledge proxies need not be varieties; research scale/period/quality differ; falling productivity challenges a time-constant V6 a. Table7 cotton version2 rises, so preserve heterogeneous exceptions.
sources.source_discrepancy: Table7 and p1110 show −5.1% and14-year half-life; immediately preceding prose on p1134 says −5.3% and13years. Use labeled Table7 numbers, note internal inconsistency; Scite faithfully surfaced prose.

sources.title: R & D-Based Models of Economic Growth
locators: publisher abstract; qualitative specification critique only
sources.method: Time-series critique of scale effects and semi-endogenous growth model.
sources.mapping: Supports considering diminishing research productivity; does not estimate V6 a_i or factor-augmentation-to-variety elasticities.
sources.access_note: Publisher abstract verified; author PDF available but browser extraction returned no text, Scite denied fulltext. Do not attribute unverified equation locators or coefficient estimates.

sources.authors: Lawrence F. Katz, Kevin M. Murphy
sources.title: Changes in Relative Wages,1963-1987: Supply and Demand Factors
sources.method: OLS annual aggregate college/high-school log wage premium on relative labor supply and linear time trend; US CPS earnings years1963-1987; competitive two-labor CES.
sources.classification: estimated reduced-form demand trend conditional on CES model; not knowledge elasticity
sources.mapping: V6 implies Delta log(w_H/w_L)+rho*Delta log(phi H/L)=(1-rho)*(xi-nu)*Delta logN with fixed alpha/markup. Their trend cannot directly identify either V6 exponent.
sources.mismatches: College labor not V6 intermediate bundle; rho>1 reverses sign of augmentation effect relative to substitutable-skill CES. Endogenous research allocation and knowledge growth must be accounted for.

source_candidates.value: annual h=.0363 consumption, .0369 GDP; for >=15% thresholds .0218,.0192

rows.baseline_recommendation: No evidence-backed V6 point. If an exploratory center is operationally necessary, use h=.02/year as analyst-chosen scenario only, pi=(.98)^Delta; never label it an estimated technology hazard.
rows.robustness_recommendation: Hazard scenarios h=.01,.02,.04/year -> pi=(1-h)^Delta, labeled analyst grid informed by scale of macro-disaster evidence, not credible confidence interval; add event-specific bounds when technology dates exist.
rows.mapping_confidence: Low; numerical transformation high-confidence conditional on matched hazard, event match unestablished.

source_candidates.value: aH=.2 per unspecified model period; numerical illustration
research productivity growth is mostly negative; no portable level for a

rows.mapping: a=(G_N-1)/[(1-phi)H]. Annual knowledge growth g_N and constant share s_R over Delta years -> aH=[(1+g_N)^Delta-1]/s_R. If H'=cH, a'=a/c.
rows.baseline_recommendation: Recover from matched N-growth and researcher share at chosen period; pending that mapping, HKT aH=.2 may be retained solely as an illustrative initialization, not an external estimate.
rows.robustness_recommendation: Use conditional aH bounds [((1+g_N,lo)^Delta-1)/s_R,hi, ((1+g_N,hi)^Delta-1)/s_R,lo]. No literature-validated scalar interval exists; study declining-productivity alternative outside current constant-a solver.
rows.mapping_confidence: Low empirically; exact conditional accounting transformation.

source_candidates.value: single-country aH=.2 does not establish RoW level

rows.mapping: Same as US, using geography-consistent RoW innovation and research labor; pooling country levels does not produce a portable mean a.
rows.baseline_recommendation: Separate conditional data recovery; no literature point recommendation. Equal aH across countries is an imposed scenario, not evidence.
rows.robustness_recommendation: Country-coverage, research-quality and knowledge-output proxy bounds, propagated through the same exact formula.
rows.mapping_confidence: Low, additionally weakened by RoW aggregation.

rows.definition: partial log A_X,US(u,N)/partial log N=xi_u; A_X=barA_X*N^xi_u
rows.mapping: For constant scales, xi_u=Delta log A_X / Delta log N. A common multiplicative normalization of N does not change xi; changing the knowledge concept by a power does.
rows.baseline_recommendation: HKT .7 only as transparent illustrative initialization, jointly with nu=.2. Empirical baseline remains unset pending factor-augmentation/knowledge-growth mapping.
rows.robustness_recommendation: Joint intervals obtained by propagating plausible A_X,A_L,N growth estimates; report equal or reverse growth scenarios if data support them, even though current solver excludes xi<=nu. No literature-backed box bound.
rows.mapping_confidence: Definition high for HKT comparison, numerical empirical transfer low.

rows.definition: partial log A_L,US(u,N)/partial log N=nu_u; A_L=barA_L*N^nu_u
rows.mapping: nu_u=Delta log A_L / Delta log N, jointly with xi_u and the same N proxy. Not BJRW diminishing-returns beta or annual technology growth.
rows.baseline_recommendation: HKT .2 as illustrative initialization only; empirical baseline unset.
rows.robustness_recommendation: Joint growth-ratio confidence/scenario region. Do not infer range from xi>nu>0 theorem; preserve zero/reversed evidence separately from solver admissibility.
rows.mapping_confidence: Definition high for HKT comparison, numerical empirical transfer low.

independent_derivation: V6 w_H/w_L=theta*alpha/(1-alpha)*(A_X/A_L)^(1-rho)*(phi H/L)^(-rho). Constant theta and alpha imply the wage-growth residual mapping used above.
